chapter_title: Open Curation Pipelines — CCNet, C4, Dolma, FineWeb
course_outline_concepts: CCNet three-stage: language ID → perplexity filter → dedup; why it's still the conceptual skeleton
C4 heuristic filters: bad-word list, terminal punctuation, javascript stripping; the line-dedup step
Dolma per-source pipelines (web vs code vs peS2o) and the full filter-ablation table
FineWeb-Edu classifier-based quality: Llama-3 annotation → classifier training → score threshold
How to read and critique a new pipeline: what filters, in what order, with what thresholds, ablated how

sources.what_to_extract: Three-stage pipeline (langID → dedup → perplexity); KenLM-against-Wikipedia as the quality signal; multilingual scope; why this became the template.
Heuristic stack from T5: bad-word blocklist, terminal-punctuation rule, javascript-line stripping, language filter, three-sentence line dedup; the biases that followed.
Six-stage cascade (URL → doc dedup → langID → quality → content/PII → paragraph dedup); per-source pipelines (web vs peS2o vs Stack); ablation-driven filter defense; the dolma toolkit.
15T-token recipe with trafilatura + per-dump MinHash; the classifier-trained-on-Llama-3-annotations pipeline for FineWeb-Edu; score≥3 keeps 8% of FineWeb; classifier > heuristic stacks.
Quality as a scaling variable; effective-sample-size framing; two corpora with equal token count can sit on different scaling curves.
WRAP's evidence that even classical-filtered web text is noisy; rephrasing as a complement to filtering; implication for how much further filters alone can take you.
